## Personality

Susan is a spinster residing in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen). She is described as having a grim-faced demeanor while simultaneously possessing a kind-hearted nature.

## History

Susan Baker served as hired help at [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), where her unconscious funny remarks occasionally amused visitors like Captain Jim and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md). Following the loss of Anne's first child, [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) and Susan insisted that Susan be kept on as hired help for the summer to ensure [Anne](../character/anne.md) could regain her health. Later, during a federal election, Susan joined the household in discussing political opinions as they reacted to the [Liberal](../codex/factions.md#liberal) victory. When Susan had to leave temporarily after her sister broke her leg, [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) moved in to keep [Anne](../character/anne.md) company in her absence. Upon returning late from the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), Susan brought news to the household and expressed her shock over Miss Cornelia's upcoming marriage.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed P1](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. ## Quotes

> "Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning."
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)

> "If you cannot I will not go, Mrs. Doctor, dear, Matilda’s leg to the contrary notwithstanding. I will not have you worried, and that blessed child upset in consequence, for any number of legs."
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 36 BEAUTY FOR ASHES P23](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0023)

> “Do not tell me,” said Susan fiercely, answering the anguish in Marilla’s eyes, “that God could be so cruel as to take that darling lamb from us when we all love her so much.”
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P5](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0005)

> “Now for breakfast,” she said briskly. “I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.”
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010)

> "Oh, the poor lamb—the poor lamb! How can she bear it, Miss Cuthbert? I am afraid it will kill her. She has been that built up and happy, longing for that baby, and planning for it. Cannot anything be done nohow, Miss Cuthbert?"
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P18](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0018)
